headline: Panama, Marshall Islands and Norway Object to COP31 Package
deck: The proposed text remained subject to objections from delegations before any approval could take place.
body: Panama officially rejected the Antalya Pact, along with the EU, the Guardian reported. [E7]
The Marshall Islands said it would formally object to the decision, and Norway joined the objections, according to the Guardian. [E8][E9]

COP31 President Murat Kurum had said the presidency put forward a text it believed all parties could agree on, with the conference to reconvene on Sunday morning to approve it. [E3] Associated Press reported that the text was not immediately public and that it was unclear whether negotiators had received it overnight. [E2]
This follows a deadlock, when countries remained unable to agree on a new global climate deal after negotiations ran through the night. [E6]

Reuters reported that delegations had until 0300 GMT to object, with a session scheduled at 0600 GMT to begin approval. [E4] The UN climate body says almost 200 parties own the process, with the presidency guiding it each year. [E5]
The Guardian reported that large negotiating blocs had asked the joint presidency to include a transition away from fossil fuels and restate a commitment to triple climate-adaptation finance. [E1]

evidence_box.fragment: Earlier tonight, several large negotiating blocs entered the Turkey and Australia joint presidency offices to ask that a reference to a “transition away from fossil fuels” be included in any final agreement here. They also wanted to re-state a previously agreed commitment to triple finance for climate adaptation.
